candidates.title: Use few-shot answerable/unanswerable exemplars to improve abstention on unknowable questions
candidates.rule: When you need a model to say "I don't know" on unanswerable questions, prompt with in-context examples mixing answerable and unanswerable questions rather than a bare question or an instruction alone; this matters most for non-instruction-tuned base models.
candidates.passage: This impact is particularly noticeable in the davinci model, where ICL facilitates a 27.96% improvement over the direct.
candidates.finding: Across GPT-3 (ada/babbage/curie/davinci) and InstructGPT (text-*-001) models, F1 for identifying unanswerable SelfAware questions rose from direct to instruction to ICL input forms, with the biggest gain (+27.96% for davinci) in the base model; ICL also narrowed the gap between davinci and text-davinci, suggesting the prompt supplies what instruction tuning otherwise provides. Even the best model, GPT-4, reached 75.47% F1 versus a human benchmark of 84.93%.
workloads: SelfAware: 1,032 unanswerable questions plus 2,337 answerable ones from SQuAD, HotpotQA, TriviaQA
candidates.conditions: Temperature 0.7; ICL prompt with 3 answerable and 3 unanswerable hand-written examples; uncertainty judged automatically by SimCSE similarity (threshold 0.75) to 16 reference uncertainty sentences; F1 with unanswerable as positive class.
candidates.limitations: Single paper, 2023-era models; ICL results reported only for GPT-3/InstructGPT series, not LLaMA derivatives or GPT-4; gains may partly reflect increased abstention, and the paper does not report whether added abstention hurts accuracy on answerable questions under ICL; no cost or token-budget matching; exemplars were hand-written and may not transfer to other domains.
candidates.validation_test: On your own mix of answerable and unanswerable/underspecified requests, run the same model with direct, instruction, and 6-shot mixed-exemplar prompts; measure abstention F1 on unanswerable items and accuracy on answerable items to check that ICL gains are not bought with over-refusal.

candidates.title: Detect model abstention by embedding similarity to a curated uncertainty-phrase list
candidates.rule: To score abstention automatically in free-text generations, compare sliding-window chunks of the output against a small curated list of uncertainty phrases using a sentence embedding model, and tune the similarity threshold on a hand-labelled sample rather than guessing it.
candidates.passage: The results in Table 2 indicate that a threshold of 0.75 produced the highest F1 score, balancing precision and the inclusion of other uncertain sentences.
candidates.finding: With 16 manually curated uncertainty reference sentences and SimCSE embeddings, thresholds from 0.65 to 0.95 were swept on 100 hand-labelled text-davinci-002 responses; 0.75 gave the best F1 (91.89, precision 100, recall 85), while higher thresholds lost recall and lower ones lost precision. The ablation shows threshold choice materially changes the measured abstention rate.
workloads: 100 responses to SelfAware questions, manually labelled for uncertainty
candidates.conditions: Sliding window of length 5 to split target text into semantic chunks; punctuation stripped and text lowercased; 16 reference sentences sourced from GPT-3/InstructGPT outputs.
candidates.limitations: Threshold tuned on only 100 responses from one model family; authors note the reference sentence list came only from GPT-3/InstructGPT and may miss uncertainty phrasing from other models; no comparison against an LLM-as-judge or other detectors; the 0.75 value is unlikely to transfer unchanged to other embedding models or domains.
candidates.validation_test: Hand-label ~200 of your agent's outputs as abstaining or not, sweep the similarity threshold for your embedding model and phrase list, and compare resulting F1 against an LLM-judge baseline to decide which detector to deploy.

reason: The paper compares three input forms (direct, instruction, in-context learning) across GPT-3/InstructGPT series on the SelfAware dataset, giving a testable prompting rule for abstention behaviour. It also reports an automated uncertainty-detection method with a tuned similarity threshold, usable as a harness evaluation rule. Both are narrow, single-paper, 2023-era model results.
